content: Wrap rage, also known as wrapping rage or package rage, refers to the intense anger, frustration, and sometimes violent behavior that arises when individuals struggle to open packaging that is particularly difficult to remove. In 2006, the phenomenon of wrap rage was formally acknowledged by Consumer Reports magazine, which introduced the Oyster Awards to highlight products with the most challenging packaging to open. An article in the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette discussing wrap rage was featured on The Colbert Report. During the segment, host Stephen Colbert humorously attempted to use a knife to open the packaging of a new calculator but was unsuccessful, illustrating the frustration associated with such packaging. When individuals experience wrap rage, they often resort to using tools or implements in a hasty and unsafe manner. This reckless approach is typically accompanied by the application of excessive force, which can lead to injuries. Wrap rage can result in minor physical injuries, such as cuts, bruises, or sprains to the fingers and hands. It may also cause muscle strains, particularly in the shoulder, due to the exertion of excessive effort while attempting to open stubborn packaging. In some cases, the act of opening certain types of packaging, such as blister packs, can render the product non-returnable. Many stores require returned items to be in their original packaging, which becomes impossible if the packaging has been forcibly destroyed during the opening process.
